title: Microsoft’s president warns White House against skilled immigration crackdown
key_facts: Smith, Microsoft vice chair and president, told Politico in Ireland on Wednesday that Vance's claim was 'completely off base'
Vance said at the 8 Oct press conference Microsoft laid off 6,000 US workers and gained 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards
Smith said most applications were for people already working at Microsoft, held up by the USCIS backlog
Microsoft says it hired 9,200 American workers in its last fiscal year
The Labor Department suspended eight employers from the PERM green-card step, including Microsoft, Wipro, TCS, Infosys, Adobe, HCLTech; none charged
Smith said five of the six people given tech and science medals by Trump on 8 Oct arrived as immigrants
Smith warned the ban could push companies to expand R&D outside the US
quote_evidence: Smith denied Vice President JD Vance's accusations last week that Microsoft was engaging in widespread fraud through the so-called PERM process (Newsweek).
"We hired 9,200 American workers in our last fiscal year, and that was left out of the narrative," he told Politico.
why_it_matters_hint: A major employer is pushing back publicly against a White House labour-visa action.
notes: Politico blocked (403); read Newsweek and The Indian Express reports of the Politico interview. Interview Wed 14 Oct in Ireland. Reply story: Vance's 8 Oct press conference named; not checked whether we ran it earlier.
